name: PCF8591 8-bit ADC/DAC module
description: NXP 8-bit converter with four analog inputs (successive approximation, single-ended or differential) and one analog output, controlled over I2C at address 0x48. Runs on 2.5–6 V; readings are ratiometric to VREF, which the module ties to VCC (1 LSB = VCC/256; the simulator assumes a 3.3 V supply). Sold as: PCF8591 AD/DA converter module YL-40 (header 1: SCL, SDA, GND, VCC; header 2: AOUT, AIN0, AIN1, AIN2, AIN3; on-board LDR on AIN0 via jumper P5, thermistor on AIN1 via P4, 10 kΩ pot on AIN3 via P6, 10 kΩ I2C pull-ups, A0–A2 grounded).
eli5: Gives your board four extra 'how much voltage?' inputs and one adjustable voltage output, all over two I2C wires.

pins.description: I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up on the module)

pins.description: I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up on the module)

pins.description: Analog input 1 (thermistor when jumper P4 is fitted); keep within 0 V…VCC

pins.name: AIN3
pins.description: Analog input 3 (potentiometer when jumper P6 is fitted); keep within 0 V…VCC

supplierQuery: PCF8591 AD DA converter module YL-40
buildNotes: Write the control byte (0x40 | channel keeps the oscillator and AOUT on; 0x00 | channel with AOUT off), then read 2 bytes and keep the SECOND: the first byte is the previous read cycle's result (0x80 after power-on).
Single-ended code = Vin × 256 / VREF; VREF is VCC on the YL-40, so power it from 3.3 V when used with a 3.3 V board and never put more than VCC on an AIN pin.
Pull jumpers P4/P5/P6 to free AIN1/AIN0/AIN3 from the on-board thermistor, LDR and potentiometer before wiring your own signals to them.
DAC: write control byte with bit 6 set followed by the data byte; AOUT = data/256 × VREF.

driver.code:
# PCF8591 8-bit 4-channel ADC + 1-channel DAC (NXP PCF8591 datasheet Rev. 7)
# I2C address 0x48 (1001 A2 A1 A0, all tied low on the YL-40 module).
#
# Control byte (datasheet Fig. 4):
#   bit 6    analog output (AOUT/DAC) enable
#   bits 5-4 input programming (00 = four single-ended inputs)
#   bit 2    auto-increment
#   bits 1-0 A/D channel number
# A conversion starts after each read-address acknowledge, so the FIRST byte of every
# read is the result of the PREVIOUS read cycle (0x80 after power-on). We read two bytes
# and keep the second, which is a fresh conversion of the channel just selected.
# Single-ended code = (Vin - VAGND) / Vlsb, Vlsb = (VREF - VAGND) / 256.

ADDR = 0x48
_AOUT_EN = 0x40


class PCF8591:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=ADDR, vref=3.3):
        # On the YL-40, VREF is wired to VCC and AGND to GND: pass the module's supply voltage.
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        self.vref = vref
        self._ctrl = 0x00  # single-ended, AOUT off (power-on state)
        self._dac = 0

    def read(self, channel):
        """Raw 8-bit code (0-255) of AIN<channel>, single-ended."""
        if not 0 <= channel <= 3:
            raise ValueError('channel must be 0-3')
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([self._ctrl | channel]))
        b = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 2)
        return b[1]

    def read_voltage(self, channel):
        """AIN<channel> in volts (0 V to vref - 1 LSB)."""
        return self.read(channel) * self.vref / 256

    def write_dac(self, value):
        """Set AOUT to value/256 x VREF (0-255) and enable the output buffer."""
        self._dac = max(0, min(255, int(value)))
        self._ctrl |= _AOUT_EN
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([self._ctrl, self._dac]))

    def dac_off(self):
        """Switch AOUT to high impedance (lowest supply current)."""
        self._ctrl &= ~_AOUT_EN
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([self._ctrl]))

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from pcf8591 import PCF8591

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
adc = PCF8591(i2c, vref=3.3)  # YL-40: VREF = VCC
while True:
    c = [adc.read(ch) for ch in range(4)]
    print('AIN0=%d AIN1=%d AIN2=%d AIN3=%d' % tuple(c))
    print('V0=%.2f' % adc.read_voltage(0))
    time.sleep_ms(500)
